status: proposal only; original production and public film unchanged
title: Egregopathy
spine: Make institutional continuity visible through an explicitly imagined factory whose reporting omits downstream harm, use costly correction as the mechanism, and turn the book’s critique of its own selected evidence into a second reason to read rather than another diagnostic disclaimer.

source.scope: Full chapter map and prior complete 20-line script; complete source-1,2,4,6,7,8,36,37,38 read, with longer sections in contiguous bounded ranges. Not the whole book or an external reference audit.
source.genre: Proposed institutional analytical concept with historical synthesis and substantial self-critique; not a psychiatric diagnosis.
source.images: All four non-cover figures inspected (pages18,39,103,118). Adapt moral-distance and correction-route relationships as an inhabited factory/river process. Omit generic loop raster and speculative biological-divergence staircase; the latter also has clipped embedded text and does not serve this short introduction.

scenes.title: The objective keeps its office
lines: Egregopathy asks why replacing harmful leaders can leave an institution's behavior unchanged.
Its proposed concept describes harm protected by roles, targets, and selective information.
The book treats this as institutional design, not a psychiatric diagnosis.
It asks whether moral concern can change objectives when correction costs something.
scenes.emotionalPlan: Ordinary confidence meets unsettling continuity; the people remain recognizable and conscientious, not villains.
scenes.artPlan: Open close inside a factory management office: an ordinary manager signs a production target while completed goods continue along a visible delivery track. A successor enters with a different face and coat, takes the same instructions, and the track keeps moving. The retained target sheet stays attached to the actual machine control schedule, not floating as a slogan. Pull slightly wider to reveal an incomplete information route from outside the office; reserve the full downstream consequence for scene 2. A report is a work object, not a second heading. Warm ochre machinery, teal uniforms and river blue establish a lived setting. This is an authored hypothetical applying source-6, not a claim about any named company.

scenes.title: What never reaches the report
lines: Take its opening image of a company poisoning a river.
Imagine its managers seeing revenue reports while a downstream household loses usable water.
Different departments defend production, legal compliance, and reputation through separate measures.
An apology changes the message, while the discharge continues unchanged.
The book's test is whether evidence of harm can constrain that process.
scenes.emotionalPlan: Widening the frame makes the hidden cost concrete; frustration becomes a specific question about authority.
scenes.artPlan: A panoramic cutaway connects the same factory's discharge pipe to a river beside a downstream household. An adult reaches for water, notices the visibly discolored flow and withdraws the empty container; no bodily injury or specific contaminant is depicted. At the factory, actual shipment totals reach production and revenue review, while a resident's report stops at a claims clerk whose role cannot alter the target. Three workers perform distinct tasks within the same workplace, rather than three isolated icon cards. The public apology changes on a notice board, but a moving discolored flow continues into the river. Do not turn this into proof about real departments or measured pollution. Labels identify only necessary work objects and actual authority relationships.

scenes.title: A true example can still mislead
lines: The historical chapters trace a disturbing pattern across very different forms of organized power.
The book later challenges the evidence it selected to make that pattern persuasive.
Accurate examples can mislead when contrary examples remain outside the frame.
Institutions also create public health, shared resources, scientific knowledge, and constraints on powerful actors.
That counterhistory tests whether the proposed concept explains more than its dramatic language suggests.
scenes.emotionalPlan: The confident pattern becomes uncomfortable self-examination, then a more generous view of collective action.
scenes.artPlan: Change scale and medium completely: a moving editorial crop extracts the factory harm from a larger illustrated historical spread. Every selected example remains visibly accurate, but the crop repeatedly leaves constructive collective work outside. Then the spread unfolds to reveal a staffed clinic, people maintaining a common irrigation channel, and a researcher consulting preserved observations; develop these as small inhabited environments rather than symbol rows. An editor moves the crop to compare the missing context with the chosen case. No fabricated counts or claim that the constructive cases cancel harm. Use plum binding, warm coral editorial marks and vivid civic scenes. This adapts the final chapter's selection critique; it is a nonfiction argument, not a protected fiction twist.

scenes.title: Concern needs authority
lines: Readers gain two investigations: how institutions resist correction, and how arguments recruit belief.
The Moral Turing Test asks what an institution's apology makes impossible afterward.
Imagine authority pausing that harmful production, accepting a cost rather than changing only its language.
The Book as a Small Egregopath then questions the argument's own selective framing.
Read it to examine that mechanism while testing the boundaries of the explanation itself.
scenes.emotionalPlan: Conditional agency replaces fatalism; end curious about the book's two-sided investigation rather than morally triumphant.
scenes.artPlan: Return to a close physical process rather than the whole office: in an explicitly imagined test, the same resident evidence now reaches a decision-maker with authority over the production control. The decision-maker pauses the harmful operation; the shipment track stops with an uncompleted order still visible. This enacts a cost-bearing constraint, not an empirical success story, permanent cleanup, universal reform guarantee or operational factory procedure. Existing discoloration in the river does not instantly disappear. End with the book opened to its two real chapter headings and a small continuation of the paused mechanism, avoiding duplicate large headings. Preserve the whole subtitle lane and keep people/labels clear during evidence travel. No invented fines, compensation amounts, contaminant data or diagnosis.

evidence.heading: A Note on the Claim
evidence.quote: Egregopathy is a proposed analytical concept, not a clinical diagnosis and not a recognized psychiatric category.

evidence.heading: A Note on the Claim
evidence.quote: It describes a recurring group-level pattern in which persons outside a protected boundary are treated instrumentally, harm is separated from decision authority, moral language becomes easier to produce than costly correction, and objectives persist even as the people occupying institutional roles change.

evidence.heading: Prologue - The Crime With No Criminal
Prologue - The Crime With No Criminal
evidence.quote: One department measures profit. Another handles compliance. Another manages public relations. Another processes claims. Another signs procurement orders. Another moves numbers across a spreadsheet.

evidence.heading: Prologue - The Crime With No Criminal
evidence.quote: What no part necessarily contains is the whole consequence.

evidence.heading: A Name for the Thing
evidence.quote: Imagine a corporation in which every executive personally prefers not to injure customers, yet each also faces a narrow metric.

evidence.heading: A Name for the Thing
evidence.quote: Replace the employees and the pattern can remain.

evidence.heading: The Moral Turing Test
evidence.quote: It asks whether moral information can reliably alter the organization's behavior when doing so imposes a real cost on a central objective.

evidence.heading: The Moral Turing Test
evidence.quote: Does evidence of harm change targets, budgets, incentives, or decision rights?

evidence.heading: The Moral Turing Test
evidence.quote: If the people who understand the harm can only recommend, while the people who control the objective are rewarded for preserving it, the lesion remains.

evidence.heading: The Moral Turing Test
evidence.quote: A credible conscience should sometimes destroy an option the organization wanted: abandon a product, release damaging evidence, compensate outsiders, accept slower growth, surrender jurisdiction, stop a weapons program, close an unsafe facility, or allow a critic to remain inconveniently employed.

evidence.heading: The Moral Turing Test
evidence.quote: Whenever an institution claims to have learned, ask what became impossible afterward. An apology is evidence about language. A new constraint is evidence about architecture.

evidence.heading: The Category Error
evidence.quote: The first nine chapters selected slavery, empire, mass violence, institutional betrayal, corporate misconduct, polarization, and AI misalignment because those cases make the egregopathic lens vivid. They are real. The selection is also profoundly non-random.

evidence.heading: The Category Error
evidence.quote: Public health systems eradicate disease. Courts can constrain private revenge. Democratic institutions can enable peaceful transfer of power. Corporations can coordinate technologies too complex for individuals. Scientific institutions preserve cumulative knowledge. Insurance pools risk.

evidence.heading: The Book as a Small Egregopath
evidence.quote: No factual claim becomes false because it was selected. But selection changes belief.

evidence.heading: The Book as a Small Egregopath
evidence.quote: If every fact presented is true but all disconfirming facts are systematically omitted, the resulting model can be radically false in proportion.

evidence.heading: The Book as a Small Egregopath
evidence.quote: The second surviving claim is architectural: moral concern must be coupled to control.

evidence.heading: The Book as a Small Egregopath
evidence.quote: Humanity's history is not only the scaling of predation. It is also the scaling of correction.

technicalBoundaries: Factory and downstream household are explicitly imagined extensions of the opening river example, not a named reported event.
Only one necessary early clinical-status statement; later limit is the concrete selective-evidence critique.
Paused production is a hypothetical cost-bearing test, not a reported reform, permanent cleanup, or engineering procedure.
No personal psychiatric attribution, biological-divergence claim, chemical measurement or health outcome.
Institutions also enable constructive collective action; examples do not cancel the harm or validate the novel concept.
supersedesDefects: Previous office-to-intact-house line never showed actual harm or why it failed to affect authority.
Repeated diagnostic qualifications displaced the substantive final chapter’s critique of case selection.
